{
  "findings": [

      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 79,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry.datetime",
      "body": "The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first non-empty optimized page raises TypeError when build_cursor computes a key, and any non-zero cursor would also filter a datetime column with a numeric value. This makes the optimized pagination path fail with 500 or invalid queries. Use DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator handle datetime conversion."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 880,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing",
      "body": "When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code sets start_offset to the negative offset and executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this raises an AssertionError rather than performing efficient reverse pagination. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client input, a crafted cursor can trigger a 500 on endpoints using this paginator. Negative offsets should be rejected or handled without negative QuerySet slices."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 182,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "BasePaginator change allows invalid negative offsets for prev cursors",
      "body": "The new start_offset calculation uses cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers, so a cursor like 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:stop], which Django QuerySets do not support, leading to a 500 on any BasePaginator-derived endpoint. For non-prev cursors, negative offsets are silently coerced to 0, which can mask malformed input and return the wrong page. Cursor offsets should be validated as non-negative."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 891,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Extra-row drop condition compares against an impossible length",
      "body": "In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing from start_offset, results can contain at most limit + extra rows, but the code checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When cursor.offset is greater than zero, this condition cannot be true, so the extra row fetched for backward pagination may not be removed. This can return one too many rows or produce incorrect prev-cursor state. The check should compare against the number of rows actually requested, e.g. limit + extra or stop - start_offset."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Typo order_b prevents changing queryset ordering",
      "body": "In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently lost, so previous-page pagination can query in the wrong order and return incorrect results. This affects BasePaginator and its subclasses used by the new optimized path."
    },

At minimum, tests are needed for the optimized audit-log endpoint covering empty and non-empty pages, next and prev cursors, malformed or negative offsets, and permission fallback when optimized_pagination is absent or the user lacks access. Without tests, these failure modes are easy to regress."

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate AuditLogEntry.datetime
findings.body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. Unlike DateTimePaginator, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the field value and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first non-empty optimized page raises TypeError when build_cursor computes a key, and any non-zero cursor would also filter a datetime column with a numeric value. This makes the optimized pagination path fail with 500 or invalid queries. Use DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator handle datetime conversion.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, the code sets start_offset to the negative offset and executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this raises an AssertionError rather than performing efficient reverse pagination. Because cursor offsets are parsed from client input, a crafted cursor can trigger a 500 on endpoints using this paginator. Negative offsets should be rejected or handled without negative QuerySet slices.

findings.title: BasePaginator change allows invalid negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The new start_offset calculation uses cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor.from_string accepts negative integers, so a cursor like 0:-1:1 causes queryset[-1:stop], which Django QuerySets do not support, leading to a 500 on any BasePaginator-derived endpoint. For non-prev cursors, negative offsets are silently coerced to 0, which can mask malformed input and return the wrong page. Cursor offsets should be validated as non-negative.

findings.title: Extra-row drop condition compares against an impossible length
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing from start_offset, results can contain at most limit + extra rows, but the code checks len(results) == offset + limit + extra. When cursor.offset is greater than zero, this condition cannot be true, so the extra row fetched for backward pagination may not be removed. This can return one too many rows or produce incorrect prev-cursor state. The check should compare against the number of rows actually requested, e.g. limit + extra or stop - start_offset.

findings.title: Typo order_b prevents changing queryset ordering
findings.body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns to queryset.query.order_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The intended ordering change is silently lost, so previous-page pagination can query in the wrong order and return incorrect results. This affects BasePaginator and its subclasses used by the new optimized path.

findings.title: No tests for the new pagination path
findings.body: The PR introduces a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch and a new paginator with cursor, datetime, and negative-offset behavior, but no tests. At minimum, tests are needed for the optimized audit-log endpoint covering empty and non-empty pages, next and prev cursors, malformed or negative offsets, and permission fallback when optimized_pagination is absent or the user lacks access. Without tests, these failure modes are easy to regress.
